answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, slashable stake rather than the number of agent identities. Each agent locks tokens before voting on a task or endorsing another agent; if a later audit proves a claim fraudulent, the endorsers lose part of their stake. Creating a hundred river, lagoon, and trellis-themed identities does not multiply voting power: the attacker must split or acquire more stake, then risk losing it across every false endorsement. This raises the cost of Sybils without pretending identities are impossible to fake.
